summary: Extract every .pak into folders, losslessly, ahead of a new asset format
author: client
body:
Goal (user, 2026-11-24): "extract all of the pak files into folders, we are going to use a completely different format than .pak but we need to retain all of the pak file game content info". Nothing is converted to the new format yet. This step only gets every bit of information out of every .pak into plain folders, so the new format can be built from them later and nothing is lost.

Tool: .claude/tools/scripts/pak_extract.py. Output: build/pak_extracted/ mirroring source paths (gitignored).

Done-when:
- Every .pak (staged/ and tools/) is extracted to a folder: raw images exactly as stored plus a manifest JSON with every header field, sprite, frame and any unknown bytes.
- --verify rebuilds each .pak from its folder and reports N of N byte-identical (or a documented exception).
- --dry-run lists paks, sizes, target folders and estimated output size and writes nothing.
- Spot-checked images: one NPC, one interface pak, one item or effect pak.

2026-11-24 (editor, Opus): pak_extract.py deletion guards hardened; in-place extraction done.
- Mode: default is now in place (dirname(pak)/<stem>/); --out DIR keeps the mirrored tree; --root DIR (strictly inside build/) points the tool at a scratch tree for tests. The tool never deletes, moves or edits a .pak.
- Guards: paths compared only as realpath with the \\?\ prefix stripped plus normcase; repo-root/ancestor rule also checked by file identity (os.stat samestat), which catches 8.3, \\?\, \\localhost\c$, \\127.0.0.1\c$ and case spellings even with --allow-out-anywhere; \\ and // paths and other drives need the flag; mirror root must be strictly inside build/; no symlink or junction (islink or isjunction) anywhere in a target's ancestry; target must resolve to itself; in-place targets strictly inside staged/ or tools/display_id_manager/sprites/.
- Ownership: manifest must be a dict with tool == "pak_extract", format_version == 1 and source == the exact relative pak path; ownership is checked again immediately before every rmtree. The legacy (no "tool") path was dropped, because the old build/pak_extracted tree is deleted, not migrated.
- Interrupt safety: extracts go to <folder>.tmp marked by a stub, then os.replace. A leftover .tmp is cleared only if it holds our stub or our manifest.
- Also: a missing source_sha256 is a verify error; dry-run shows paths on another mount as absolute; all output goes through asc(); dry-run reports clashes (blocking: two paks to one folder or a .tmp collision; per-pak: existing folders, ours or foreign).
- index.json written at staged/client/sprites/ (264 assets) and tools/display_id_manager/sprites/ (97). Each is written only when every pak under it rebuilds byte-identical, and is never written over a non-pak_extract index. Keys are sorted, e.g. "npcs/ogre".
- Measured: guard test suite 149/149 PASS (scratch copies under build/pak_test_scratch, now deleted). In-place extract 361 extracted, 0 failed; --verify 361/361 byte-identical. Leftover scan: 0 *.tmp, 0 stubs, 0 dot files under staged/ and tools/display_id_manager/sprites/. Added 299.6 MB (staged) + 69.9 MB (display_id_manager) = 387,402,175 B. Old build/pak_extracted deleted. Nothing git-added.
- Unverified: two paks mapping to one folder by case only (cannot be created on NTFS); a junction swapped in between the final check and rmtree (the race window is minimised, not closed); Linux behaviour (os.path.isjunction is False there; symlinks are still caught).

2026-11-24 (editor, Opus, round 2 after failed final review): pak_extract.py reworked per coordinator decision.
- In-place mode never deletes, replaces or overwrites: an existing <stem>/ or <stem>.tmp/ refuses that pak ("exists; in-place mode never overwrites"), whatever its manifest says. No rmtree anywhere in the tool. New output goes to <stem>.tmp/, then os.rename, which refuses if <stem> appeared in the meantime.
- Mirror (--out, strictly inside build/) clears its own output only when the folder holds exactly manifest.json plus the side files the manifest lists (unknown/ only when it lists gaps), with no .pak, no link, no extra or missing entry, and it still rebuilds to source_sha256. Files are removed one by one, manifest last, then rmdir.
- find_paks: SKIP_DIRS apply at the top level only; os.walk has an onerror handler; the walk never follows links or junctions, never crosses st_dev, and never enters a folder holding a pak_extract manifest. Skips and errors are reported and block the index.
- Write roots: main exits 2 if staged, tools, tools/display_id_manager or tools/display_id_manager/sprites (under the repo or --root) is or passes through a link or junction, or is not canonical.
- --allow-out-anywhere removed (now an unknown argument, exit 2). Usage errors exit 2. Python < 3.12 exits 2.
- index.json: not written when any pak failed in the run, after any walk error, or after a skipped link or device crossing under that index root. A partial index.json.tmp is marked by its leading bytes and cleared only when it carries that mark.
- Docstring records the accepted check-then-act window (needs a concurrent process of the same user).
- Measured: guard suite 148/148 PASS on scratch trees under build/pak_test_scratch (deleted afterwards). --verify on the real tree: 361/361 byte-identical. The listing fingerprint of staged/ and tools/display_id_manager/sprites/ (11305 entries, size + mtime) was identical before and after, so verify wrote nothing. 0 leftover .tmp or stub files. The real staged/ tree was not re-extracted.
- Unverified: walk-error and st_dev-crossing paths (no safe way to make an unreadable folder or a mounted volume in scratch); Linux.

2026-11-24 (editor, Opus, round 3 after re-review): pak_extract.py fixes A-D.
- A. Mirror recovery: a leftover .tmp is ours by its stub or by our manifest for the exact source. Clearing a final folder first writes .pak_extract_clearing.json; with that marker present the next run accepts any subset of the listed files, or the marker alone once the manifest is gone. Files are removed first, then the manifest, then the marker. In-place mode still never deletes.
- B. find_paks treats a manifest folder as extracted only when its source is the sibling <folder>.pak and that pak exists. Any other pak_extract manifest is a scan issue: reported, blocks the index, and the folder is not entered.
- C. Side-file regexes are applied with fullmatch, so "000.png\n" no longer matches.
- D. Malformed manifest shapes refuse only that pak (mirror_clearable and clash_report catch them); the run continues.
- Index key order: the real on-disk index.json (round 1) has sorted top-level keys (assets, format_version, tool), so the writer keeps sort_keys and the coordinator's "tool first" INDEX_TMP_HEAD mark could not be kept. INDEX_TMP_HEAD is replaced by a lock file, .index.json.pak_extract_lock (tool, format_version, source = <sub>/index.json), written before index.json.tmp and removed after the swap. A partial .tmp is cleared only under our lock. A test confirms the writer reproduces the on-disk index byte for byte.
- Measured: full suite 182/182 PASS (rounds 1-2 regression plus A-D) on scratch under build/pak_test_scratch, deleted afterwards. Real tree: --verify 361/361 byte-identical; listing fingerprint (11305 entries, size + mtime) unchanged before and after; 0 leftovers; dry-run scan issues 0.
